answer: An identity posts 30 credits to the tide ledger and must show work in three tide windows. Each completion is key-signed and hashed into the lantern ledger, which refuses a hash claimed by another key. At dawn, auditors check the windows: work clustered in one window, or a reused hash, burns the bond. The k-th identity pays 5(k-1) extra, so the 1,000th fake pays 5,025 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,527,500. An honest agent pays 30 once, recovered after its third window. A rented-window ring fails: a completion signed by another key cannot match the claimant key, so the dawn audit burns the bond.
